# Integral midpoint defects do not control boundary-martingale transport
obstruction. This is not a counterexample to OC or to the necessary
conditions at an attained minimizing family.

## 1. Precise statement being disproved

For a lattice-complete finite base \(P\), let
\[
 E(P)=\{(p,q,m):p,q\in P,\ p\ne q,\ m=(p+q)/2\in P\}.
\]
For a convex function \(\phi\) on the real base space, put
\[
 \delta_{pqm}(\phi)=\frac{\phi(p)+\phi(q)}2-\phi(m)\ge0.
\]
Even for equal full-dimensional actual fibers, no-heavy-fiber sources,
the actual entire boundary-area measure \(\eta\), and a normal-preserving
physical martingale from a positive source \(\nu\) to \(\eta\), it is
false that the convex-potential gap can always be bounded by a finite
nonnegative combination of integral midpoint defects:
\[
 \int\phi(z)\,d(\eta-\nu)
 \ \le\ \sum_{e\in E(P)}c_e\delta_e(\phi),\qquad c_e\ge0.       \tag{1}
\]
The counterexample below has strictly positive left side and every
defect on the right equal to zero. Thus arbitrary finite, family-dependent
coefficients, or coefficients multiplied by fiber-volume credits, do
not repair (1). In particular restricting the right side to triangulation
edges does not repair it.

The source can additionally be represented by three equally budgeted
actual closed cap indicators which cover the full ambient space.
Those caps are pure-integer caps, and are not claimed to be maximizing
depth certificates or proper critical caps at a shape minimum.

## 2. Actual lattice-complete body

Write
\[
 v_1=(1,0),\quad v_2=(0,1),\quad v_3=(-1,-1),\quad
 Q=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}.
\]
The three inequalities of \(Q\) are
\[
 x+y\le1,\qquad -2x+y\le1,\qquad x-2y\le1.                  \tag{2}
\]
The convex hull is contained in \([-1,1]^2\). Substitution of the nine
integer points in that square in (2) gives exactly
\[
 B=Q\cap\mathbb Z^2=\{0,v_1,v_2,v_3\}.                    \tag{3}
\]
Their four residues modulo 2 are distinct.

Fix \(d\ge1\) and let \(K=[0,1]^d\). The full-dimensional compact
polytope
\[
 C=Q\times[0,2]\times K\subset\mathbb R^{3+d}
\]
has precisely the twelve integer bases
\[
 P=B\times\{0,1,2\}.
\]
Every actual fiber is exactly \(K\), of volume 1. Consequently the
total mixed volume is 12, and the number of occupied parity classes
is \(k(P)=4\cdot2=8\). Every fiber has volume
\[
 1=\frac23\,\frac{12}{8}<\frac{12}{8},                     \tag{4}
\]
so no fiber is heavy even for the occupied-parity target.

Every distinct pair in \(P\) whose midpoint is integral must have the
same \(B\)-coordinate, by (3), and third coordinates 0 and 2. Thus,
up to exchanging endpoints, there are exactly four edges in \(E(P)\):
\[
 ((b,0),(b,2),(b,1)),\qquad b\in B.                        \tag{5}
\]

## 3. Exact boundary source and martingale

Let \(\sigma\) be the boundary-area measure of \(K\), marked by its
outward unit normal. Explicitly it is the sum of the ordinary
\((d-1)\)-dimensional measures of its \(2d\) facets, marked by
\(\pm e_i\). Their overlaps are null. For \(d=1\), the two endpoints
carry counting measure. In every case
\[
 \tau=\sigma(\partial K)=2d.
\]
Define the actual target measure
\[
 \eta=\sum_{p\in P}\delta_p\otimes\sigma.
\]
Define a source on this same marked boundary by densities
\[
 \frac{d\nu}{d\eta}(b,j,x,u)=
 \begin{cases}
 2,&b=0,\\
 2/3,&b\in\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}.
 \end{cases}                                             \tag{6}
\]
Here \(j\in\{0,1,2\}\), and \(x,u\) are unchanged in the following
transport.

For each \(j,x,u\), send the source density 2 at \((0,j,x,u)\)
as density 1 to itself and density \(1/3\) to each
\((v_i,j,x,u)\). Send each source density \(2/3\) at
\((v_i,j,x,u)\) to itself. Then each target origin has density 1,
and each target vertex has density \(2/3+1/3=1\). Thus the target
is exactly \(\eta\), with no discarded boundary mass.

The source-origin probability row has weights \(1/2,1/6,1/6,1/6\).
Its base barycenter is the origin because
\(v_1+v_2+v_3=0\); its third coordinate, continuous point, and normal
are unchanged. All other rows are diagonal. This proves the physical
martingale identity and normal preservation directly. In particular,
Jensen's inequality proves every normal-localized convex-order
inequality satisfied by this coupling, not just one potential test.

The nontrivial anchored template
\[
 (0,j)=\frac13(v_1,j)+\frac13(v_2,j)+\frac13(v_3,j)          \tag{7}
\]
is a rational extreme representation: its three support points are
affinely independent. It is active for every continuous normal,
since all fiber support functions equal \(h_K(u)\). The transport
is therefore consistent with the audited rational-template
factorization and with actual common ambient supporting planes.

## 4. Zero midpoint defects and positive transport gap

Use the globally convex physical potential
\[
 \Phi(z,x)=\phi(z)=z_1^2+z_2^2.
\]
It is constant along every column in (5); hence
\[
 \delta_e(\phi)=0\quad\text{for every }e\in E(P).           \tag{8}
\]
In each of the three layers the origin contributes zero to the
potential, and each donor has target-minus-source density \(1/3\).
Since \(\phi(v_1),\phi(v_2),\phi(v_3)=1,1,2\),
\[
 \int\Phi\,d(\eta-\nu)
 =3\tau\frac{1+1+2}{3}
 =4\tau=8d>0.                                            \tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) disprove (1) with every integral midpoint edge
available. They also give a linear obstruction: the signed base
flux changes the total mass of the four columns, whereas every
signed midpoint-edge credit from (5) has column total zero.

## 5. An exact cap-incidence representation, with its scope

In the full ambient space define three closed halfspaces
\[
 H_1=\{2z_1-z_2\ge0\},\quad
 H_2=\{-z_1+2z_2\ge0\},\quad
 H_3=\{-z_1-z_2\ge0\}.                                   \tag{10}
\]
Their normals sum to zero, so they cover every ambient point:
the three displayed expressions cannot all be negative. At \(b=0\)
all three inequalities are equalities. At \(v_i\) exactly \(H_i\)
holds, strictly, as direct substitution shows. They are independent
of \(j,x,u\). Hence (6) is exactly
\[
 \nu=\sum_{i=1}^3\frac23\,1_{H_i}\eta.                    \tag{11}
\]
Each cap contains six whole fibers and has actual mixed volume 6,
which is half the total. Thus its common normalized budget is
\(\beta=1/2\), and the sum of the three weights is
\(2=1/\beta\). The boundaries carry all three origin fibers;
(11) uses closed indicators and retains that boundary mass.

This observation does not turn the example into an attained-minimum
certificate. These are pure-integer caps with no proper continuous
section. Their budget is not asserted to be the maximum-depth
budget. No selected critical-center circuit conditions or their
universal cap-choice quantifiers are asserted. What is disproved is
the midpoint-defect charging implication from the geometric,
arithmetic, and transport data in Sections 1--4, even with the
additional elementary cap properties in this section.

## 6. The actual family is safely above its OC target

Let \(g=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\) and \(y=(0,1,g)\in S\). The three-fiber
column
\[
 T=\{0\}\times\{0,1,2\}\times K
\]
is centrally symmetric about \(y\), and has mixed mass 3.
For every closed ambient halfspace containing \(y\), reflection
about \(y\) pairs each point not in the halfspace with a point in
it; any boundary mass increases the included mass. Therefore
\[
 \mu(S\cap H)\ge\mu(T\cap H)\ge3/2,\qquad
 \operatorname{depth}_S(y)\ge1/8.
\]
For \(d\ge1\), \(\gamma_d\le1/2<1\), so this is strictly larger
than \(\gamma_d/8\). In particular this obstruction is not an OC
counterexample.

For every \(n\ge3\), pad the body by \([0,1]^{n-3}\) in integer
coordinates and repeat the coupling in every binary layer. There
are \(12\cdot2^{n-3}\) fibers, exactly \(2^n\) occupied parity
classes, the strict ratio in (4) is unchanged, every midpoint
defect is still zero, and the gap in (9) is multiplied by
\(2^{n-3}\). The same single-column lower bound gives depth at
least \(2^{-n}>\gamma_d2^{-n}\).

## 7. Dependencies and what remains available

The obstruction has a direct finite proof. It uses no unproved
arithmetic inequality, no midpoint-component closure, and no
variational attainment. The rational-template theorem is only
used to identify the obstructed route; its conclusions are
verified directly in this example.

This does not disprove the actual midpoint mass-growth
inequalities D3/D5. Those retain forced volume in integer output
fibers. It disproves using only midpoint Jensen defects to pay
for every allowed normal-preserving transport gap. Higher-arity
anchored relations such as (7) contain information absent from
all integral midpoint defects on the same complete base.

The independent verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_midpoint_defect_boundary_transport_coherent.py enumerates
the exact bases, parity classes and edges, checks the rational
martingale and cap-incidence matrices, and verifies the potential
gap with exact arithmetic.
